label: Crew models
description: Who operates the unit, and how many players that takes. Passenger seats are counted separately, so any crew model can also carry passengers. That covers the brief's 'transport with passengers' (shown on the card whenever there are passenger seats) and IFVs that have both a gunner and passengers.

terms.label: Solo
terms.description: One player moves, aims and uses abilities.
examples: Titanfall: one pilot runs the Titan, which fights on its own when the pilot gets out
PlanetSide 2: the Lightning light tank is built for one player
terms.source_rule: In-game for a unit with one player seat in the source (a MechWarrior mech, a PlanetSide 2 Lightning). The proposal for every unit without player seats unless driver-gunner, squad or remote applies. A crew named in lore or voice lines does not change it.

terms.label: Driver + gunner
terms.description: Two operating seats: the driver moves (and may fire the main gun), the gunner mans a turret. Each weapon records which seat fires it; the solo fallback says what a lone player can do.
examples: Battlefield and PlanetSide 2 battle tanks: the driver fires the main gun, a second seat mans a top gun
C&C Renegade: the driver drives and the gunner fires; alone, the driver fires too
Foxhole light tanks: the driver only drives, a separate seat fires the main gun
Halo Warthog: driver, turret gunner and a passenger
terms.source_rule: In-game when the source has a driver seat and a separate gun seat. As a proposal, only for a vehicle, walker, hover or aircraft of medium size or bigger, never a power suit, that fires two weapons at the same time from separate mounts. A separate mount aims on its own: a roof gun, a gun on the front or side of the hull, a second turret. A gun that turns with the main gun is the same mount. These do not count: weapons swapped by a mode or toggle; weapons the source picks by target type (one for ground, one for air), which fire one at a time; weapons added by an upgrade, a passenger or a kill; and point defence that fires by itself. If the source doesn't say whether two weapons fire together, count them as one at a time. The driver keeps the main weapon and any gun that turns with it. Each other weapon on its own mount that fires at the same time as the main weapon goes to the gunner, and every other weapon stays with the driver (decision 2A; see armament[].seat).

terms.label: Driver + gunner + commander
terms.description: Adds a commander seat that spots and marks targets, sees further, and triggers abilities or a secondary weapon.
examples: Foxhole battle tanks: driver, gunners, a commander with a better view, and an engineer who reloads and repairs
Battlefield 3 main battle tanks: the CITV Station unlock opens a third seat, a commander with zoom, thermal vision, laser designation and a motion sensor but no weapon
terms.source_rule: In-game only, when the source has a separate seat that spots, marks or commands, or a crew seat that only loads, repairs or runs systems. A gunner seat whose loadout swaps its gun for spotting tools is still a gunner. Never proposed for a unit without player seats.

terms.label: Squad
terms.description: One player leads a small group (a leader with AI followers, or a pack of tiny drones) that moves as one; losing members weakens it before it dies.
examples: Company of Heroes: infantry squads share one health bar but lose firepower as soldiers die
terms.source_rule: In-game when the source moves two or more soldiers or tiny drones as one unit for their whole life, with one order and a shared fate (Company of Heroes or Dawn of War squads). Units bought in pairs that then act alone are solo.

terms.label: Remote operator
terms.description: The player pilots a remote body while their own soldier stays parked and vulnerable; losing the remote returns them to that soldier.
terms.source_rule: Only when the source has a person who stays on the field, outside the machine, while steering it (a soldier who parks to fly a drone). A note in the lore that the machine was once remote-controlled does not count.

tie_breaks.rule: A unit with player seats copies them, however many weapons its one pilot fires. For a unit without player seats, count what the source unit does, not what its text says: two weapons firing at the same time from separate mounts make driver-gunner (its coding rule says what doesn't count); anything else is solo. Faction flavours never decide a source unit's crew; they only weight generated cards.
Remote only when an operator stays on the field in the source. Otherwise an uncrewed machine is solo.
